summary: The Clarendon Fund is the University of Oxford's flagship graduate scholarship. It offers over 200 new, fully funded scholarships a year for master's and DPhil courses in every subject, with no restriction on nationality or residence, and there is no separate application: you are considered when you apply for your course by its December or January deadline.
meta_title: Clarendon Scholarship 2027 at Oxford: eligibility and deadlines
meta_description: Clarendon pays full Oxford fees and a living grant for any master's or DPhil, open to all nationalities. How you are considered and the 2027 deadlines.
covers: Course fees in full, for Home and Overseas fee status students.
A grant for living expenses of at least the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate for full-time scholars: at least £20,780 in 2025–26.
Funding for the course's period of fee liability; some divisions add a further period with the living grant only.
Part-time scholars receive a smaller study support grant towards non-fee costs.
eligibility: Any nationality and any country of residence.
Applicants for a new full-time or part-time master's or DPhil at Oxford, in any subject.
You must apply by the December or January deadline that applies to your course.
Not eligible: holders of a deferred offer, and current students continuing the same degree.
how_to_apply: Choose your Oxford course and check its deadlines on the graduate course page.
Apply for the course by its December or January deadline. There is no Clarendon form and nothing extra to send.
Your department nominates candidates, and the academic divisions shortlist them in February or March.
Successful candidates are emailed, most by the end of April. If you have heard nothing by mid-June, you have not been awarded one.
watch_out: It is highly competitive: Oxford says most scholars have at least a first-class degree or equivalent, such as a GPA of 3.7 out of 4.
A course's final January deadline counts, but applying by an earlier deadline can bring an earlier decision on your place.
Some Oxford courses charge an application fee; check your course page for waivers.
